title: Column priority heatmap and graceful collapse affordance for virtual tables
creator: Ariella Chen
description:
Background: Our virtualized table component currently asks product teams to choose a single density profile and manually pin or hide columns. Customers building data-heavy UIs report unpredictable column collapse behavior and poor discoverability when screen real estate is constrained.

Problem: When tables compress at narrow widths or in small containers, important columns are often hidden without clear indication. Manual pinning is too heavyweight for many use cases. There is no visual signal that helps users and engineers reason about which columns should remain visible as space is constrained.

Proposal: Design a lightweight column-priority heatmap and a graceful collapse affordance that: (1) computes an intuitive priority score for columns based on metadata (importance tags, sort/filter presence, recent interactions), (2) displays a subtle heatmap overlay in the header to communicate priority to users, and (3) animates a predictable, reversible collapse behavior that preserves context and accessibility. This should integrate with existing density tokens and the virtualized rendering pipeline so perceived performance remains snappy.

Goals:
- Provide clear visual guidance to users about column importance without adding clutter.
- Enable default, non-destructive collapse behavior that avoids hiding high-value columns.
- Surface hooks for product teams to set column importance via schema or prop, while providing a sensible automatic fallback.
- Ensure accessibility: screen-reader announcements for collapse/restore and keyboard-first controls for pin/unpin.

Constraints:
- Must work with virtualized rendering (no full-table reflow during normal collapse/restore).
- Animations should be GPU-friendly and limited to transform/opacity.
- Design tokens must map to current density scale (compact, default, roomy).
- Should not increase runtime overhead significantly; heavy computation should be precomputed on the host thread or done incrementally in ENG layer.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap UI spec in Figma with token-mapped colors and low-contrast mode
Interactions defined for: auto-collapse, manual pin/unpin, keyboard restore, and hover affordance
Accessibility spec: SR announcements for column collapse/restore and focus management flows
Edge cases documented: pinned columns, multi-row headers, column groups, and inline editors
Implementation handoff with ENG including batching considerations and perf budget (<=8ms extra compute per resize event)
Design tokens updated or new tokens proposed if needed and documented in tokens.md
design_notes: Priority algorithm: base score = explicit 'importance' attribute (0-3) + recentInteractionBoost + sortOrFilterBoost + pinnedBoost. Normalize to 0-100 for UI mapping.
Heatmap visual language: 4-step opacity scale using existing color token 'surface-ink/level-2' with alpha ramps; avoid saturated hues to keep table readable.
Collapsed behavior: softly fade and translate columns out with a 140ms ease-out; replaced cell content should have skeleton placeholders when restored until virtualization resumes.
Tokens impact: propose new tokens: 'table.priority.heatmap.0' .. 'table.priority.heatmap.3' and 'table.collapse.transition-duration'
Telemetry: emit events for auto-collapse decisions and user overrides to inform future defaults
decisions: Prefer subtle monochrome heatmap over colorful gradients to reduce cognitive load for dense tables
Auto-priority will be the default; products can opt out by setting all explicit importance attributes
Keyboard mapping: Alt+Shift+Left/Right to cycle pin/unpin when focus is on header cell
Performance requirement: priority computation should be debounced and limited to columns in viewport
